slides.title: Leasing Platform Decision — Saudi Arabia
slides.subtitle: SaaS vs platform vs custom build | Comparison & recommendations | 30 September 2026 | Prepared by Basir — ARKAN Research
slides.notes: Prepared for internal evaluation. All findings verified against public sources as of 30 Sep 2026; pricing is quote-based and must be validated in RFP.

slides.title: Executive summary — the right answer depends on which leasing business you run

bullets.text: Governing thought: no single platform wins — Saudi regulatory fit (ZATCA + Tajeer) decides short-term rental; ERP-grade lifecycle decides corporate leasing
Short-term car rental → local Saudi-native SaaS or configured local build (Tajeer + ZATCA Phase 2 native)
Corporate operational + finance leasing → Annata A365 or CarPro LeaseProXL via formal RFP
Custom build → only if leasing is a strategic differentiator AND a 3-year owning team is committed
CarPro: deepest lease pedigree (LeaseProXL, 1M+ vehicles claimed) — but now mid-merger (Emotion, Mar 2025): get written roadmap first
Rentey (Qoad): thinnest evidence base — include only after 2+ same-size operator references

slides.notes: Answer-first slide. Three scenarios drive three different winners; no vendor clears every Saudi regulatory gate natively.

Market signals

• SAR 7.5bn (FY23) → 11.7bn (FY28E), 9.2% CAGR — Aljazira Capital

slides.notes: Sources: Research&Markets 2026-2031 report (USD 3.07bn 2026, CAGR 7.09%); Aljazira Capital Transportation Outlook (SAR basis). Growth drivers: tourism 30mn Hajj/Umrah target, Vision 2030 mega-projects, corporate fleet outsourcing.

slides.title: Three regulatory gates decide the winner: ZATCA, Tajeer, SAMA

bullets.text: ZATCA Fatoora Phase 2 — API integration for clearance/reporting, cryptographic stamp + QR; waves now down to SAR 1M turnover; Wave 24 (SAR 375K) cited for 2026 — verify against ZATCA
Tajeer (Transport General Authority) — mandatory unified e-contract registration for car rental: 1.77M contracts issued in Q4 2025 alone; API setup SAR 15,000 + ~SAR 2.25/tx
SAMA — finance lease is a licensed activity (Finance Companies Control Law + Finance Lease Law M/48): capital, governance, outsourcing/cloud non-objection
PDPL + sector rules — GDPR-style law, BUT SAMA/CST/NCA keep regulated financial workloads effectively in-Kingdom; confirm hosting explicitly with any SaaS
Language & identity — Arabic-first contracts and UI; Absher/NAFATH e-signature flow is the Tajeer completion path
Consequence: international platforms clear these only with middleware — local SaaS and custom builds clear them natively

slides.notes: Any option that cannot produce ZATCA-compliant invoices and Tajeer-registered contracts on day one shifts work onto your team or blocks go-live. Shariah structuring note: ijara contract mechanics differ from interest-based markup modules — software must model ownership-transfer schedules; verdicts to qualified scholars.

slides.title: Part II — The Four Options
slides.subtitle: Who they are, what they prove, what to verify
slides.notes: Each option slide: identity, strengths, red flags. Evidence standard: 2+ independent sources per load-bearing claim.

slides.title: CarPro (now Emotion) — deepest operational-lease pedigree, now mid-merger

bullets.text: Founded 1992 · HQ Amsterdam · rental + leasing + subscription modules; clients incl. Hertz, Europcar, LeasePlan, VW Financial Services (vendor claim)
LeaseProXL: lease quotations, flexible invoicing (corporate/combined), AR + aging + collections, cashiers, multi-currency, fleet status
Scale claim: 85+ countries, 1M+ vehicles, 500+ deployment partners
RED FLAG — ownership churn: sold to Ibérica (Jul 2020) → merged with Jimpisoft/Rentway into Emotion Mobility (Mar 2025); product-line consolidation underway
RED FLAG — no native ZATCA/Tajeer/Absher layer; requires middleware or local integrator

slides.notes: Sources: carprosystems.com (products/leaseproxl, company), CFI Group deal notice 2020, Auto Rental News merger release Mar 2025, CB Insights. Ask in RFP: written Rentway-vs-CarPro roadmap, reference customers of similar fleet size.

slides.title: Rentey (Qoad) — promising all-in-one SaaS, but the thinnest evidence base

bullets.text: Positioned as all-in-one rental platform: reservations + payments, built-in CRM, fleet optimization, analytics, mobile access
Sits in Qoad's product family (QFleets for corporate car sharing) — vertical SaaS vendor
RED FLAG — public footprint limited to a single vendor product page: no verifiable customer references, funding, or headcount found (extraction blocked)
RED FLAG — no public evidence of ZATCA, Tajeer, or SAMA awareness; Arabic/localization status unknown
Verdict: do not shortlist without proof — request 2+ same-size operator references and a live sandbox

slides.notes: Source: qoad.com/en/products/rentey (vendor page, single source — low confidence). Comparably-positioned tools exist in the same price class (Rently, Renthub); if Rentey cannot evidence Saudi readiness, alternatives exist.

slides.title: Annata A365 — ERP-grade leasing on Dynamics 365; strongest at enterprise scale

bullets.text: Founded 2001 · HQ Kópavogur, Iceland · 15 offices / 4 continents · Microsoft Inner Circle ISV (top 1% of Dynamics partners)
A365 = ERP + CRM + DMS industry solution on Dynamics 365 F&O; Rental & Subscription modules cover cradle-to-grave vehicle lifecycle
Enterprise integration: finance (GL, fixed assets), audit trails, Copilot/Azure ecosystem; MEA delivery via partners (SHEA, Confiz — 2025 partnership)
D365 ships a Saudi ZATCA e-invoicing localization (CSID onboarding path) — but integration work is on the implementer
CAUTION — no Riyadh office; Saudi delivery depends on partner quality. Verify D365 KSA reference implementations in RFP

slides.notes: Sources: annata.net (contact, solutions/rental), craft.co, LinkedIn, sheaglobal.com, Confiz release Sep 2025, Microsoft Learn D365 Saudi e-invoicing onboarding. Best fit where leasing must integrate with enterprise finance and SAMA-grade audit.

slides.title: Custom build — total control and Saudi-native compliance, at a price

bullets.text: Full control: own schema, own roadmap, ijara-compatible contract modelling, no per-seat licence tax, exit = your choice
Native compliance possible from day one: ZATCA Phase 2 APIs, Tajeer + Absher/NAFATH, Arabic-first UI, PDPL in-Kingdom hosting
TCO logic: custom wins 5-year view ONLY if maintained (budget 15–20%/yr of build cost) by a durable team — else it decays into legacy
Reality check: leasing-core build (contracts, SAMA reporting, fleet lifecycle, billing) = multi-million-SAR, 6–12+ month programme; generic ERP numbers ($18–60K) do NOT transfer
Vendor-independence risk disappears; team/key-person risk appears — bus factor 2+ on every core module

slides.notes: Sources: ACM 2025 case study (SaaS vs IaaS ERP TCO), sitepoint custom-vs-OTS analysis, CISIN TCO framework (vendor-adjacent, framing only). Honest test: is leasing logic your differentiator, or is speed to market the differentiator?

shapes.text: For AlMajdouie's corporate leasing ambition: run the RFP between Annata A365 and CarPro LeaseProXL (+ one local compliance integrator), with custom build held as the strategic option behind a capability gate, not as the default.

slides.notes: Recommendation logic: buy commodity, build differentiation; custom only when owning maintenance for 3+ years. Rentey excluded from shortlist pending references.

slides.title: Decision ask — approve scenario-led shortlisting and vendor due diligence

bullets.text: 1. Approve the scenario framework (this deck) as the basis for platform choice
2. Commission formal RFP: Annata A365 + CarPro LeaseProXL + 1 local integrator (4–6 weeks)
3. Demand from each vendor: 2+ same-size KSA/GCC references, sandbox PoC on OUR data, exit clauses in writing
4. Verify SAMA scope + ijara structuring with counsel/scholars before any finance-lease module decision
5. Confirm ZATCA wave position + Tajeer scope with ZATCA/TGA directly (current: waves to SAR 1M; Wave 24 cited 2026)
6. Decide build-vs-buy only after RFP results — with the 3-year ownership test applied

slides.notes: Ask: management approval to run the RFP (owner: IT Application Management; timeline: 4-6 weeks; decision date: placeholder). Nothing is committed beyond due diligence spend at this gate.
